_meta.deliverable: sport profiles - swimming, aquatic, endurance and track
_meta.authority_order: coach round-2 answers (COACH-R2) > round-1 answers (COACH-ANSWER) > everything else
_meta.trigger: coach request 2026-10-08: 'all of the different popular sports in the United States ... Include swimming as well' (and swimming is the first sample plan he will grade - COACH-R2 GEN-07)
_meta.schema: 04_profiles.json profile schema (field names kept); new fields listed in new_fields; field names aligned with synthesis/sports/team.json so the merge is mechanical
_meta.consistency: 04 profiles reused unchanged where they existed (track_sprinter, track_jumper, distance_runner); 04 variants built out (track_400, track_thrower with a class correction); weekend_warrior is the base of every recreational profile (GEN-02 / ATH-13). Coach-approved numbers reused: sprinters 75 % plyometric and 2 aerobic sessions (R2-ATH-01 / 06), pre-season 2 aerobic (R2-ATH-06), in-season 2 lifting days (PER-08) and 2 aerobic (ATH-07), weekend warriors 50 % (R2-ATH-01).

evidence_tags.SCIENCE: external literature or official calendars, cited in references

_meta.unit: working sets per week (04 convention); athletic doses in contacts / throws / cuts / metres; conditioning in sessions per week by colour
_meta.baseline_phase: off-season build week, mid-block (04 convention); season_overrides give pre-season (~60 %) and in-season (~40 %) weeks
_meta.stairway: every block climbs like a stairway: smaller steps in the first weeks, slightly bigger after the halfway point, the hardest weeks last (12-week: last 4 weeks 'brutal'); 'start at a 2, end at an 11' = perceived effort / overall load, not set counts; no deload or maintenance week inside a block (COACH-R2 PER-03/04/05, VOL-07)
_meta.check_in: no check-in = the plan follows its planned stairway (COACH-R2 VOL-03); no lifestyle inputs (sleep / stress / job / yardage) - the coach rejected them (COACH-R2 GEN-04); the step is decided from effort, completion and pain only
_meta.no_bands: no bands, chains or variable resistance anywhere (EQ-01 / EQ-12) - swim dryland traditionally uses bands; every prehab rule here uses DB, KB, cable, machine, plates or bodyweight
_meta.build: scratchpad aet/build.py (common.py, budgets.py, texts.py, refs.py, specs_*.py) reading synthesis/04_profiles.json
_meta.id_note: the two 04 profiles are reused unchanged (merge = enrich in place); the three 04 variants of track_sprinter become full profiles here (merge = promote the variant); every other id is new. Picker ids from generator_spec_v1 F11 are mapped in picker_map; proposed extra picker values: high jump, pole vault, javelin, cross country, indoor / gravel cycling

profiles.name: Swimming - sprint (50-100)

picker_map.second_choice: main stroke -> variants (free / back / breast / fly / IM)

profiles.template: 3 dryland days (A knee + pull / B hip + push / C full) + 1 optional Focus day; pool sessions around them

days.note: dryland days; pool sessions are the sport

profiles.weekly_sets_note: off-season build week, mid-block (04 convention); pre / in-season weeks in season_overrides; muscle targets from the volume engine

plyo.phases: landings first (RC1), then single responses from a start-like position (RC2), short repeated hops (RC3); Receive-Create stages: 12-week plan RC1 Land wk 1-3, RC2 Land & Go wk 4-7, RC3 Repeat wk 8-12; 8-week plan 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8; restart at stage 1 each off-season; stay at the current stage in maintenance blocks; L2-L3 may start at stage 2 (COACH-R2 ATH-03)
tracks: JUMPING ANKLE (pogo / ankle hops) for bone loading
lists: ballistic = squat jumps, box jumps, broad jumps, loaded / hex-bar jumps, medball throws (COACH-R2 ATH-02)
plyometric = pogo / ankle hops, hurdle hops, depth jumps, bounds, squirrel jumps, repeated jumps (COACH-R2 ATH-02)

throwing.notes: overhead and slam throws mirror the streamline / catch; rotational throws for long-axis strokes; keep overhead throws off heavy-pull pool days (INFERRED)

triple_ext.ceiling: hang clean / power clean; single-arm DB snatch (barbell snatch L2+ with healthy shoulders)
triple_ext.level_note: names are L2+ defaults; L1 = DB / KB snatches, single-arm DB snatch, KB squat clean, hang clean, hang pulls, hex-bar jumps (COACH-ANSWER ATH-10 + R2-LIB-07); older / injured / high-volume clients: no snatch variants (EQ-03); 60+: none by default (R2-ATH-08)

resistance.rep_zone: STRENGTH 3-5 + POWER (VOL 1 -> VOL 2 -> VOL 3 one per block, PER-11); hypertrophy only where the coach adds size
resistance.pairing: knee + pull / hip + push (UNI-11, ORD-06); same-pattern pairing for L2+ (UNI-06)
priorities: posterior cuff / scapular stabilisers (rear delts own sets)
avoid: barbell snatch / overhead squat when shoulder pain is flagged (EQ-03 logic)
anything that leaves the swimmer sore for the next pool session (INFERRED)
resistance.sets_bands_status: descriptive only - generator muscle targets come from the volume engine (12 / 03; floor 10 sets per muscle - COACH-R2 VOL-04/06, see open question O1)

core.mode: anti-extension (streamline / dolphin) and anti-rotation first, then controlled rotation
core.dose: 2 exercises x 2 sets, light, short of failure, first in every session as the warm-up (COACH-ANSWER ATH-11, COACH-R2 SES-03); movable after the plyos or the strength block; core supersets / monster sets may be added anywhere by the coach or user (COACH-R2 SES-03)
core.slots_note: core exercises per week at 2 sets each (2 per session x main days)

formats: pool sets prescribed by the swim coach (not generated)
optional land Orange 20-40 min (any erg, EQ-14) in the transition block

pre_season.length_weeks: 4-6, length modifiable, + a 1-2-week taper before the first game / meet / race (volume -40-60 %, intensity kept, no new exercises)
pre_season.evidence: COACH-R2 PER-06 (4-6 weeks at about 60 % of off-season sets, more speed and power, 1-2-week taper; modifiable); category factors PROPOSED, resistance factor solved so the week lands at about 60 % (floor 0.25); core and calves follow the number of lift days (core 2 x 2 per session - R2-SES-03; calves 3 sets per leg day - VOL-17)

in_season.olympic: light piece 2 x 3 (hang power clean or DB snatch) on 1-2 gym days; dropped in heavy competition weeks (COACH-R2 ATH-04)
in_season.evidence: COACH-ANSWER PER-08 (about 2 lifting days, low volume); COACH-R2 ATH-07 spacing (hard day >= 48 h before competition); factors PROPOSED (about 40 % of off-season sets; with 1 lift day use about 25-30 %)

season_overrides.post_season: transition = a maintenance block (length chosen and extendable); at its end the user is asked: keep maintaining / change plan / start a training block (COACH-R2 PER-06, VOL-07)
season_overrides.no_mid_block_deload: no deload or maintenance week inside a block; a block that cannot be finished is cancelled -> maintenance -> a new block (COACH-R2 VOL-07)
season_overrides.supersedes: 04 v1 season multipliers for these sports (COACH-R2 PER-06 / ATH-07 are newer and rank higher)

variants.name: Freestyle (front crawl)
notes: base profile = freestyle; long-axis rotation -> transverse core (anti-rotation first, then rotation) and thoracic rotation mobility
flip-turn push-off ~0.3 s (AQ2) -> ballistic squat / box jumps from a deep start position

variants.name: Backstroke
notes: backstroke start = pulling up into the wall then a backward hip extension -> hip-thrust / back-extension power (BALL from a supine-like start is not possible: use broad jumps and hip-dominant ballistics)
anterior shoulder takes the catch in end-range extension / external rotation: posterior cuff + controlled end-range strength, no ballistic behind-the-body throws

variants.name: Breaststroke
notes: 73-75 % of breaststrokers report knee pain (AQ4): frontal-plane unilateral work (lateral lunge, Cossack), Copenhagen plank and hip internal-rotation range every week (KNEE_MEDIAL_KICK)
frontal / transverse share of unilateral work 25 % (vs 10 % base)
the kick is a narrow, powerful knee extension: quad strength (split squat, leg extension isometrics) without deep loaded valgus

variants.name: Butterfly
notes: dolphin kick + simultaneous overhead recovery: highest low-back extension and shoulder load (AQ4) - anti-extension core first, non-axial hinge (back extension to neutral, reverse hyper) for trunk-extensor endurance, no loaded end-range extension
one less overhead-press set (shoulders already loaded overhead in the stroke)

variants.name: Individual medley (IM)
notes: all four strokes: base freestyle profile + the breaststroke hip / knee block + the butterfly low-back rules
IM swimmers are usually middle-distance (200 / 400 IM) - pick the event group first, then this stroke variant

profiles.rationale: Sprint races are decided by power off the block and walls plus stroke force: lower-body maximal strength and jump power explain 55-73 % of start performance (AQ6), and strength at 85-100 % 1RM plus plyometrics improve turns (AQ5). Sprinters need the longest power preparation (AQ40). The pool already supplies the aerobic work, so dryland is strength, power, shoulder health (AQ3) and bone loading (AQ8).
confirm: swimming class 4 (40 % plyometric) - approve? (ground contact = block / wall pushes)
0 extra aerobic sessions for swimmers by default (pool is the aerobic work)
sprint swimmers lean bilateral (55/45 mid-block) unlike land athletes - approve?
v1_adjustments: COACH-R2 rules applied: plyo share by ground contact (ATH-01), lists (ATH-02), Receive-Create stages (ATH-03), Olympic up to 4 x / week (ATH-04), 3-5-rep full lifts (ATH-05), pre-season ~60 % + taper (PER-06), in-season spacing (ATH-07), older / youth (ATH-08), stairway (PER-03/04/05), no mid-block deload (VOL-07), tests start / end only (PER-07), core-first 2 x 2 (SES-03), spine 2-day rule (SES-01/02), 2-4 exercises per muscle on full-body days (SES-05), no lifestyle inputs (GEN-04)

ground_contact.label: long
ground_contact.typical: no ground contact in the race: the decisive pushes are the block start (time on the block ~0.70-0.77 s - AQ1) and wall push-offs on turns (~0.3 s, longer contact = more push-off force - AQ2) - both slow stretch-shortening (> 0.25 s, S32) = the 'long / stance-block' class
ground_contact.evidence: class INFERRED from block / wall contact times (AQ1, AQ2, S32); the rule that contact time sets the plyo : ballistic split is COACH-ANSWER ATH-01, approved per sport in COACH-R2 ATH-01 (swimming not on the approved list - PROPOSED)

bilateral_unilateral.upper_body: same logic for pressing / pulling (UNI-03); alternating DB rows / presses count as unilateral (UNI-07)
bilateral_unilateral.evidence: PROPOSED on the COACH-ANSWER UNI-02 scale: block starts and wall push-offs are two-footed pushes ('bilateral is more for driving and creating forces' - UNI-02); unilateral kept for hip / low-back health; in-season minimal bilateral (UNI-10) applied softly because the sport itself is not unilateral (INFERRED)

profiles.contra_ipsi: neither is a race driver: contra / ipsi lunges and step-ups are HEALTH accessories for hips and low back, mostly in weeks 1-4 of a block (CAT-13 size / strength logic); the kick start is a staggered stance, so split-stance ballistic jumps and RFE split squats count as start-specific (INFERRED)
profiles.in_season_content: maintenance of strength + start / turn power (low-volume ballistic jumps, light Olympic piece - PER-08, R2-ATH-04); shoulder care every lift

olympic_policy.rule: everyone in athletic training gets Olympic lifts (COACH-ANSWER ATH-10)
olympic_policy.pattern_split: clean variants on knee / squat days, snatch variants on hip / hinge days - cleans read as more squat-pattern, snatches more hinge-pattern; up to 4 exposures a week (COACH-R2 ATH-04)
olympic_policy.reps: full squat cleans / snatches 3-5 reps per set at the same weekly reps, coach's eye on speed (COACH-R2 ATH-05); DB / KB and pull variants may use the 4 x 8 @75 % -> 4 x 4 @90 % ramp (PER-09)
olympic_policy.load_guidance: RIR / RPE; explained as power output; % only for competitive Olympic lifters, which is its own programming (COACH-R2 GEN-06)
olympic_policy.pre_season: kept, fewer sets, faster - more speed and power (COACH-R2 PER-06)
olympic_policy.in_season: light 2 x 3 (hang power clean or DB snatch) on 1-2 gym days; dropped in heavy competition weeks (COACH-R2 ATH-04)
olympic_policy.contrast: French contrast / complexes for L2+ in the off-season only, heavy lift about 78-85 % (ATH-12)
olympic_policy.youth: floor lifts from about 14, after one block of hang work (COACH-R2 ATH-08)
olympic_policy.older_60_plus: none by default; offered as an option with the warning 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means' (COACH-R2 ATH-08); older / injured / high-volume clients never get snatch variants (EQ-03)
olympic_policy.sport_note: starts = triple extension from a staggered stance; cleans and hex-bar jumps transfer best; snatch variants single-arm DB first (shoulder load), barbell snatch only for L2+ swimmers with healthy shoulders (INFERRED)

medball_policy.types: overhead throws and slams (streamline / catch line), rotational scoop tosses for long-axis strokes; 4-8 lb; overhead throws kept off heavy-pull pool days
medball_policy.level: low (INFERRED - swimming is not on the ATH-05 list)
medball_policy.loads_lb: passes / rotations 8-10 (speed), slams 10-20, overhead 6-10, sit-up throws 6-8; never over 20 lb; lighter for youth and older clients (COACH-ANSWER EQ-06)
medball_policy.no_ball: plyo push-ups (pressing), fast cable rotations or the 'fake medball slam'; never band chops (COACH-ANSWER EQ-07)

medball_policy.aesthetics_rule: not an aesthetics profile, so throws may stay in the main workout (COACH-ANSWER ATH-05: none for aesthetics)
medball_policy.counts_as: ballistic side of the plyo : ballistic split (04 / BRAIN 9.6)

in_season_gym.typical_competitions_wk: 1-2 dual / invitational meets a week in season; championship meets at the end (AQ10, AQ11)
in_season_gym.default_pattern: Saturday meet: lifts Monday (harder) and Wednesday (short power / maintenance); Friday = rest or 10 min activation
in_season_gym.game_heavy_evidence: swimming is not on the COACH-R2 ATH-07 list; meets give no land jumps or sprints, so gym jumps are NOT halved for that reason - they drop only because of the in-season volume cut (INFERRED)

taper.pool: the swim coach tapers the pool; the tool only tapers dryland

in_season_gym.intake: COACH-R2 GEN-05 + PROPOSED championship meet date (open question O4)

rules: pull sets at least 1.5 x push sets every dryland week; horizontal pull before vertical pull (ORD-01); rear delts get their own sets (VOL-17)

posterior cuff and scapular work 2-3 x / week with DB, cable or KB: side-lying DB external rotation, prone floor Y / T raises (R2-LIB-07), KB face pulls as shoulder work on pull / shoulder days (R2-LIB-04, LIB-10) - never bands (EQ-01)

pressing = push-up variations (hands on bench = foundational, feet on bench = advanced - R2-LIB-05), neutral-grip DB or landmine press; overhead pressing low volume and seated (seated machine shoulder press - R2-LIB-07) when needed; no behind-the-neck pressing (INFERRED)

the pool is part of the load: when a check-in shows effort 9-10, missed sessions or shoulder pain, the approved check-in table holds the step or removes a set (COACH-R2 VOL-01); with no check-in the dryland stairway runs as planned (COACH-R2 VOL-03) - no yardage or lifestyle questions are asked (COACH-R2 GEN-04)
pec-minor / thoracic mobility in the warm-up; a stiff, rounded posture plus tight pec minor is a known risk sign (AQ13)
'Felt a PAIN' at the shoulder -> COACH-ANSWER VOL-03 (cut that pattern 30-50 %, move it to machines or split grips) and tell the swim coach / a professional
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ3, AQ13, AQ16) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED from the 04 SHOULDER_* rules and COACH-ANSWER VOL-17 / EQ-01 / R2-LIB-04 / R2-LIB-07

rules: core first every session as anti-extension / anti-rotation (dead bug, plank, hollow hold) before any dynamic or extension work (ATH-11, R2-SES-03)
heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days; non-axial hinge (hip thrust, back extension to neutral, reverse hyper), leg press or belt squat on the other days (COACH-R2 SES-01/02)
no loaded end-range spinal extension (no hyperextension past neutral, no heavy good-morning grinders) for athletes with extension pain (INFERRED)
hip-flexor length and glute strength every week so extension comes from the hips (INFERRED)
a young athlete with one-sided low back pain on extension -> stop the extension work and refer (health screen - COACH-R2 GEN-03)
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ4: about 76 % lifetime low back pain in competitive swimmers, butterfly / breaststroke highest; AQ14: divers up to 89 % lifetime, spondylolysis; AQ23 pole vault) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED + COACH-R2 SES-01/02

rules: hip internal-rotation range and hip strength every week: lateral lunge, Cossack lunge, Copenhagen plank (GROIN_ADDUCTOR), hold-between-knees squats (UNI-12 frontal / transverse unilateral list)
quad strength through a pain-free range: split squats, step-ups, leg extensions / isometric holds (slow, heavy) 2 x / week
avoid deep loaded valgus positions; knees track over toes on all squats and lunges (INFERRED)

the tool asks no kick-volume or yardage questions (COACH-R2 GEN-04): frontal-plane plyos stay low-amplitude for breaststrokers and polo players, and knee pain reported in a check-in moves the share / swaps exercises (VOL-03, UNI-02)
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ4: 73-75 % of breaststrokers report knee pain; AQ16: eggbeater kick loads the medial knee and hip) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED

rules: keep some jumping all year even when the plyo share is low: ballistic jumps (squat / box / broad / hex-bar - R2-ATH-02) plus a small low-amplitude block (pogo / ankle hops) 2-3 x / week
heavy compound lifting (squat, deadlift, loaded carries) every off-season block
progress impact gradually with the Receive-Create stages (COACH-R2 ATH-03); older clients follow COACH-R2 ATH-08 (no plyos by default; landings and low ankle hops OK)
injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ8: swimming is not osteogenic and a 9-month jumping programme improved bone in adolescent swimmers and cyclists; AQ30: road cyclists show low bone density, strength training helps)

rules: COACH-ANSWER VOL-03: cut that muscle or pattern 30-50%, move it to machines or split grips, keep it moving - or drop the exercise altogether if it is too much

swap fixed-grip barbell/bar -> DB/KB/handles in the same pattern; swap bilateral -> unilateral in the same pattern (MASTER_MODEL athletic A6); keep the sets ideally, 'but you have to adjust accordingly' (UNI-08)
pain moves the bilateral : unilateral share (UNI-02)
'Felt a PAIN' -> swap within the category or lower the level (GEN-05 RIGHT); if twice in a slot: swap, then cut sets, then drop a library level (INFERRED order)
all prehab uses DB, KB, cable, machine, bodyweight or plates - never bands, chains or variable resistance (COACH-ANSWER EQ-01, EQ-12)
'Coppenhaggen Plank' (R47 / O165) 3x/week pre-season, 1-2x/week in-season
adductor-integrated chops / Pallofs ('Hold object Adducted between knees'); banded adduction variants are out of scope (no bands, EQ-01 / EQ-07)
frontal / transverse unilateral work (lateral lunges, cossacks, lateral step-ups) - UNI-12
injury_prehab.extension: sports added: breaststroke / IM swimmers, water polo (eggbeater; AQ17 hip / groin pain), hurdlers, skiers.

age_notes: high school, college and pro: same plan; loads and speeds change, pros get more care for their bodies (COACH-ANSWER PRG-09)
youth: Olympic lifts from the floor from about 14, after one block of hang work; younger / growth-spurt athletes follow youth_athlete rules (COACH-R2 ATH-08, COACH-ANSWER ATH-09)

60+: no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default; offered as an option with 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means' (COACH-R2 ATH-08); landing drills and low ankle hops still fine; constrained machines for compounds and isolation (EQ-03)
more than 6-12 months off: the body is treated as L1 (PRG-05)
no rule depends on sex (ATH-09)

age-group swimmers (USA Swimming 10 & under to 15-18): pool loads are already high (AQ12) - dryland uses foundational lists (bodyweight, DB, light medball), landing skills and cuff work; floor Olympic lifts from about 14 after a hang block (COACH-R2 ATH-08)
high school / college: same plan, loads and speeds differ (PRG-09); college swimmers carry the biggest pool loads, so dryland stays 45-75 min

masters (US Masters Swimming, 18+): shoulder pain peaks at 40-60 (AQ13); bone loading and strength matter more with age (AQ8, AQ41); from 60 the older rules apply (no Olympic lifts / plyos / depth jumps by default, optional with the warning - COACH-R2 ATH-08)
equipment: full gym or DB / KB gym (often a pool-deck dryland room)
boxes for box jumps and step-ups
cable or DB for cuff work
no bands / variable resistance (EQ-01, EQ-12) - most swim dryland uses bands; every band move has a DB / cable / KB swap in 10_equipment_model

injury_prehab.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ8: swimming is not osteogenic and a 9-month jumping programme improved bone in adolescent swimmers and cyclists; AQ30: road cyclists show low bone density, strength training helps)

pain moves the bilateral : unilateral share (UNI-02)

all prehab uses DB, KB, cable, machine, bodyweight or plates - never bands, chains or variable resistance (COACH-ANSWER EQ-01, EQ-12)

Tue - hip + push: warm-up (5 min any cardio + A March / Skip / Run; A-drills never count - ORD-08) -> core 2 x 2 light (ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> medball throws + ballistic jumps (box / broad / hex-bar - R2-ATH-02) -> snatch variant (hinge pattern) -> hip thrust / back extension (non-axial) + DB bench -> single-leg RDL + DB overhead press -> loaded hip flexion (Focus) -> calves 3 sets

Fri - hip + push: warm-up (5 min any cardio + A March / Skip / Run; A-drills never count - ORD-08) -> core 2 x 2 light (ATH-11, R2-SES-03) -> plyo + throws -> snatch variant -> HEAVY DEADLIFT / trap bar 3-5 reps (axial day 2) + push -> single-leg RDL -> calves 3 sets
Sat - aerobic 2 (Orange / Green) or track session; Sun off

SHOULDER_SWIMMER.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ3, AQ13, AQ16) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED from the 04 SHOULDER_* rules and COACH-ANSWER VOL-17 / EQ-01 / R2-LIB-04 / R2-LIB-07
sports: swimming (all strokes; freestyle / fly / back highest overhead volume)
rules: pull sets at least 1.5 x push sets every dryland week; horizontal pull before vertical pull (ORD-01); rear delts get their own sets (VOL-17)

posterior cuff and scapular work 2-3 x / week with DB, cable or KB: side-lying DB external rotation, prone floor Y / T raises (R2-LIB-07), KB face pulls as shoulder work on pull / shoulder days (R2-LIB-04, LIB-10) - never bands (EQ-01)

pressing = push-up variations (hands on bench = foundational, feet on bench = advanced - R2-LIB-05), neutral-grip DB or landmine press; overhead pressing low volume and seated (seated machine shoulder press - R2-LIB-07) when needed; no behind-the-neck pressing (INFERRED)

the pool is part of the load: when a check-in shows effort 9-10, missed sessions or shoulder pain, the approved check-in table holds the step or removes a set (COACH-R2 VOL-01); with no check-in the dryland stairway runs as planned (COACH-R2 VOL-03) - no yardage or lifestyle questions are asked (COACH-R2 GEN-04)
pec-minor / thoracic mobility in the warm-up; a stiff, rounded posture plus tight pec minor is a known risk sign (AQ13)
'Felt a PAIN' at the shoulder -> COACH-ANSWER VOL-03 (cut that pattern 30-50 %, move it to machines or split grips) and tell the swim coach / a professional

KNEE_MEDIAL_KICK.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ4: 73-75 % of breaststrokers report knee pain; AQ16: eggbeater kick loads the medial knee and hip) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED
rules: hip internal-rotation range and hip strength every week: lateral lunge, Cossack lunge, Copenhagen plank (GROIN_ADDUCTOR), hold-between-knees squats (UNI-12 frontal / transverse unilateral list)
quad strength through a pain-free range: split squats, step-ups, leg extensions / isometric holds (slow, heavy) 2 x / week
avoid deep loaded valgus positions; knees track over toes on all squats and lunges (INFERRED)

the tool asks no kick-volume or yardage questions (COACH-R2 GEN-04): frontal-plane plyos stay low-amplitude for breaststrokers and polo players, and knee pain reported in a check-in moves the share / swaps exercises (VOL-03, UNI-02)

LOW_BACK_EXTENSION.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ4: about 76 % lifetime low back pain in competitive swimmers, butterfly / breaststroke highest; AQ14: divers up to 89 % lifetime, spondylolysis; AQ23 pole vault) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED + COACH-R2 SES-01/02
rules: core first every session as anti-extension / anti-rotation (dead bug, plank, hollow hold) before any dynamic or extension work (ATH-11, R2-SES-03)
heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days; non-axial hinge (hip thrust, back extension to neutral, reverse hyper), leg press or belt squat on the other days (COACH-R2 SES-01/02)
no loaded end-range spinal extension (no hyperextension past neutral, no heavy good-morning grinders) for athletes with extension pain (INFERRED)
hip-flexor length and glute strength every week so extension comes from the hips (INFERRED)
a young athlete with one-sided low back pain on extension -> stop the extension work and refer (health screen - COACH-R2 GEN-03)

RIB_STRESS.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ34: low back 15-25 % of rowing injuries; rib stress fractures a main time-loss injury, more in international rowers) for the hotspot; rules INFERRED
rules: serratus and pressing balance: push-ups / DB bench at least half of the rowing-pattern pull sets every week (INFERRED)
sudden jumps in on-water or erg volume and long low-rate / high-pressure blocks are introduced only as stairway steps, never all at once (INFERRED; COACH-R2 PER-03/04)
sweep rowers: anti-rotation core and both-side unilateral work every week (UNI-02 health use)
'Felt a PAIN' at the side of the chest -> stop rowing-pattern lifts that day and refer (INFERRED)

BONE_LOADING_NON_IMPACT.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ8: swimming is not osteogenic and a 9-month jumping programme improved bone in adolescent swimmers and cyclists; AQ30: road cyclists show low bone density, strength training helps)
sports: divers and water polo (no land impact in the sport)
rules: keep some jumping all year even when the plyo share is low: ballistic jumps (squat / box / broad / hex-bar - R2-ATH-02) plus a small low-amplitude block (pogo / ankle hops) 2-3 x / week
heavy compound lifting (squat, deadlift, loaded carries) every off-season block
progress impact gradually with the Receive-Create stages (COACH-R2 ATH-03); older clients follow COACH-R2 ATH-08 (no plyos by default; landings and low ankle hops OK)

PATELLOFEMORAL_ITB.evidence: SCIENCE (AQ25: patellofemoral pain and ITB syndrome among the most prevalent running injuries; AQ32: anterior knee pain 36 % in pro road cyclists)
rules: quad strength through a pain-free range (split squat, step-up, leg extension / isometric holds) 2 x / week
hip abductor / lateral hip strength: side lunges, lateral step-ups (LEAD_HIP_GLUTE list) every week
pain -> COACH-ANSWER VOL-03; bike-fit and shoe questions go to a professional (outside the tool - INFERRED)

wrist / forearm work (ISO_GRIP: wrist curls, reverse curls, plate pinches) 2 x / week

Extra rules for snow athletes (INFERRED): hamstring strength 2 x / week (Nordic, slider curls), heavy eccentric / isometric quad work, core strength every session, reactive balance; freestyle athletes double the stage-1 landing block. Applied by landing competency and injury history, never by sex (ATH-09).

open_questions.topic: Floor of 10 weekly sets per muscle vs athlete budgets
open_questions.detail: COACH-R2 VOL-04/06 ('I don't think anybody needs less than 10 sets a week per muscle'). Every athlete budget here leaves non-sport muscles (chest, arms, side delts, often calves in 3-day plans) below 10 - see derived.muscles_below_floor_10. PROPOSED reading (same as team.json O1): the floor applies to the muscles the athlete's plan trains for size / strength (resistance.priorities); pre-season (~60 %) and in-season (~40 %) are maintenance-like and may sit below 10. Needs the coach's yes.

open_questions.topic: Rear delts: own sets 4 / 6 / 8 vs the floor of 10
open_questions.detail: COACH-R2 VOL-04 approved rear delts at 4 / 6 / 8 own sets, but the same answer says nobody needs fewer than 10. Swimmers / water polo / javelin get 6 own sets + 0.25 credit from rows (about 7.5-8); others 4 (about 5-6). PROPOSED: rear-delt own sets count toward the floor only as 'shoulder health' work - coach to confirm whether rear delts are exempt from the floor.

open_questions.topic: Ground-contact classes for sports not on the approved R2-ATH-01 list
open_questions.detail: Approved: sprinters 75 %, weekend warriors 50 % (and the team / combat sports). PROPOSED here: swimming class 4 (40 %; block ~0.7 s, wall ~0.3 s), diving 4 (40 %), water polo 5 (25 %), high jump 2 (60 %), pole vault 2 (60 %), javelin 3 (50 %), throwers 4 (40 % - corrects the 04 variant that inherited the sprinter's class), middle / distance / XC / triathlon 1 (75 %), cycling 4 (40 %), rowing 5 (25 %), alpine skiing 4 (40 %), freestyle 3 (50 %).

open_questions.topic: Championship / goal-race date for meet and race sports
open_questions.detail: COACH-R2 GEN-05 approved 'next season start date + practice / game days'. Swimmers, track athletes, runners, triathletes, rowers and skiers peak at the END of the season, so the taper needs the main championship / goal-race date. PROPOSED: one optional extra tap for these sports.

open_questions.topic: Sport load (pool yardage, mileage) and the dryland stairway
open_questions.detail: The coach rejected lifestyle inputs (COACH-R2 GEN-04) and no check-in = no change (COACH-R2 VOL-03). So the tool does NOT ask yardage / mileage; a hard sport week reaches the plan only through the check-in (effort, completion, pain - COACH-R2 VOL-01). Flag: confirm that no 'sport volume this week' question is wanted.

open_questions.topic: Run plans other than the half marathon
open_questions.detail: The only coach running plan is the Chris Hinshaw half-marathon plan (PRG-12, COACH-R2 LIB-06); the 21.6-mile run is removed. 5K-10K, marathon, cross-country and triathlon athletes get the strength plan + 'follow your own run plan'. Should the tool offer more run plans later (coach-written)?

open_questions.topic: Borrowed half-marathon plan vs the block rules
open_questions.detail: The Hinshaw plan (used as-is) has cut-back weeks 3/6/8/12/18 and '1-mile at max effort' tests in weeks 10 and 14, while the coach's rules say no deload inside a block (COACH-R2 VOL-07) and no mid-block tests (COACH-R2 PER-07). PROPOSED: the borrowed run plan stays exactly as written; the Blaze strength block beside it follows the stairway and tests only at start and end.

04 put distance runners under 'health'. PROPOSED: a new 'endurance' group for runners, distance swimmers, triathletes, endurance cyclists and rowers (strength for economy and tissue capacity, not mass).

Swimmers, water polo players, runners, triathletes, cyclists and rowers get 0 extra gym colour sessions because their sport practice is the aerobic work (04 distance_runner rule); recreational users' own swims / runs / rides fill the 3 general sessions (ATH-07). Users can add or remove (COACH-R2 SES-06).

'Everyone in athletic training gets Olympic lifts' (ATH-10). Endurance profiles keep a small dose (2-3 sets / 1-2 exposures: hex-bar jumps, hang pulls, KB squat clean). Confirm that this low dose is what he wants for runners, triathletes and cyclists.
The rec_ profiles here (swimming, running, cycling, triathlon, rowing, ski prep) may duplicate the 'stay athletic and active' set; the merge keeps one id per activity.

open_questions.topic: 2-4 exercises per muscle on full-body days vs the 12 + 2 cap
open_questions.detail: COACH-R2 SES-05 vs SES-04 (same as team.json O2): applied as 2-4 exercises for each muscle TRAINED that day (knee + pull / hip + push pairing); athletic exercises do not count toward the resistance part. Swimming / diving / water polo 3-day plans land at about 11-12 exercises + 2 core.

references.claim: NSCA plyometric volume guide 80-100 / 100-120 / 120-140 contacts per session (Potach & Chu 2008), up to ~200 for trained adults (Chu & Myer 2013)
Nordic hamstring exercise programmes reduce hamstring injuries by up to 51% (van Dyk et al. 2019)
Strength + plyometric training 2-3x/week for 8-12 weeks improves running economy (meta-analysis)

Flanagan & Comyns 2008, Strength Cond J: ground-contact time and the reactive strength index to prescribe fast stretch-shortening-cycle (plyometric) training; fast SSC under ~250 ms vs slow SSC (Schmidtbleicher)
Sprint acceleration kinematics: faster early accelerators show shorter ground-contact times; contacts ~0.14-0.16 s in acceleration (JSSM 2003 field-sport athletes; Swansea sprint data)
Swim start: block time 0.70 +/- 0.04 s (kick start) vs 0.74 s (track start) in elite collegiate swimmers; 0.77 vs 0.80 s in another elite sample
Tumble turns: wall contact time must be long enough to build push-off force in a streamlined position (Dutch national swimmers, force plate); mean wall contact ~0.32 s in another study

Shoulder = most common injury site in competitive swimmers (prevalence 40-91%); NCAA: 34.7% (men) and 36.8% (women) of swim injuries involve the shoulder; rotator-cuff fatigue from thousands of strokes

Knee and back in swimming (Aspetar): 73% of breaststroke specialists report knee pain (75% at least 3 episodes a season); restricted hip internal rotation linked to knee pain; about 76% lifetime low back pain, butterfly / breaststroke highest (hyperextension, dolphin kick)

Systematic review, dry-land training and swim-turn performance: plyometrics 2-4 sessions/week of ~20-25 min for 6-10 weeks; strength at 85-100% 1RM, 1-6 reps, 4-5 sets improved push-off impulse and turn time

Strength and power predictors of swim starts in international sprint swimmers: 15 m start time vs CMJ peak power r = -0.85, jump height r = -0.69 (West et al.); youth: 1RM squat and jumps r = -0.75 to -0.86 with 5 / 15 m times
Taper meta-analysis (Bosquet et al. 2007; swimmers, cyclists, runners): about 2 weeks, training volume cut 41-60% exponentially, intensity and frequency kept
Swimming is not osteogenic; a 9-month jumping programme improved bone mass and fitness in adolescent swimmers and cyclists (PRO-BONE)
USA Swimming year: short course (25 yd) September-March, long course (50 m) April-early August

High-school swimming and diving: season dates are set by each state association (example: Iowa girls' season memo); seasons run about 12-16 weeks, fall (Aug-Nov) in some states or for one sex, winter (Nov-Mar) in most - INFERRED from state pages
NCAA Division I swimming and diving: conference championships mid-late February; NCAA Championships mid-late March (women one week before men)
Training volumes: elite swimmers about 40-70 km/week; youth about 38-44 km/week; 11-14-year-olds ~5 practices of 90-120 min, 14-19-year-olds ~6 x 2 h a week

Shoulder pain and disability across the lifespan of competitive swimmers: 19.4% of masters swimmers (23-77 y), more at 40-60; risk = swim exposure, prior trauma, instability, less cross-training; pec-minor tightness and low core endurance in symptomatic swimmers

Competitive divers (systematic review 2024): shoulder, lumbar spine, trunk and wrist/hand most injured; low back pain up to 89% lifetime; spondylolysis from repetitive hyperextension; more injuries on entries, back / reverse dives and platform
Springboard take-off: the board completes about 2.25-2.5 oscillation cycles before take-off; board-tip depression explains most of the hurdle flight time (long, board-timed contact)
Water polo (Aspetar): typical week = up to 5 polo sessions + 2-3 swim sessions + 3 weight sessions; overhead throwing without a stable base; eggbeater kick; heavy lifting is part of elite programmes
Water polo: high self-reported shoulder and hip / groin pain across playing levels (eggbeater during growth); up to 80% of players report shoulder pain in their career
NCAA water polo: men's championship in December (fall season), women's in May (spring season)
Energy contribution (Duffield et al. 2005): 400 m about 41/59% (men) and 45/55% (women) aerobic/anaerobic; 800 m about 60/40 and 70/30; 1500 m anaerobic only ~17-20%
Horizontal jumps (championship biomechanics): long-jump take-off contact 0.12-0.14 s; triple jump hop 0.12-0.14, step 0.13-0.15, jump 0.14-0.16 s

Athletics injuries by event group: sprinters / hurdlers / jumpers more acute (hamstring strain most common in sprints), distance runners more overuse (stress fractures, MTSS), throwers spine and upper limb; bone stress injuries ~20% annual incidence
Javelin injuries (10-year overview): shoulder ~30% of injuries; medial UCL sprain ('javelin thrower's elbow') the most common injury; also low back and knee
Preventing shoulder injuries in throwers and pole vaulters (Aspetar Sports Medicine Journal, athletics issue)
Balsalobre-Fernandez et al. 2016 meta-analysis: strength + plyometric training 2-3x/week for 8-12 weeks improves running economy in high-level middle- and long-distance runners (SMD -1.42)

Running-related injuries (Kakouris et al. 2021 systematic review): incidence ~40%; Achilles tendinopathy 10.3%, MTSS 9.4%, patellofemoral pain 6.3%, plantar fasciitis 6.1%, ankle sprain 5.8%; ITB syndrome high in prevalence
Distance runners at 14 km/h: ground contact ~0.23-0.24 s (midfoot 0.228 s vs rearfoot 0.242 s); faster / elite runners < 0.20 s
US running calendar: cross country late August-November (college championships late November); indoor track December-February/March; outdoor track March-June
Long-distance triathlon injuries (systematic review): overuse dominates (37-91%), most from the run; knee and spine the most frequent sites
USA Triathlon Age Group National Championships are held in August (Olympic and sprint distance), 4,000+ athletes
Cycling and bone health systematic review: road cyclists have low bone mineral density (lumbar spine); resistance / impact training recommended
Ronnestad & Mujika 2014 review: heavy strength training (about 2 sessions/week, 4-10RM) improves cycling and running economy / performance; 1 session/week maintains in season
Overuse injuries in professional road cyclists (Clarsen et al. 2010): 58% low back pain in 12 months, 36% anterior knee pain; clavicle the most common fracture in cyclists
Elite sprint cyclists: back-squat maximal force and power-clean maximal power the strongest predictors of on-bike force and power

Rowing injuries: lumbar / thoracic back pain and rib stress fractures typical, low back about 15-25% of rowing injuries; national-level rowers had more low back injuries, international rowers more rib stress fractures
Cumulative trauma injuries in rowing: heavy weight lifting (especially squats), missing warm-up / cool-down, high-pressure low-rate work and stroke technique named as contributing factors
2000 m rowing: about 70-80% aerobic energy; races 5.5-7.5 min; 220-250 strokes
College rowing: fall head races (e.g. Head of the Charles, October), spring 2 km sprint season from late March, NCAA Championships late May / early June
Alpine ski racing: high ACL injury rates (World Cup ~36 injuries / 100 athletes / season); 10-year youth study: 15% ACL injuries; low leg and core strength and core ratios predicted knee injury
Competitive snowboarders (national elite): back 22%, knee 16%, hand / wrist 9% of injuries; big air / snowboard cross / halfpipe riskier than slalom
US ski-club calendar example: dryland May-August and from late August, on-snow late October to mid-April (competition season)
Swim-specific dryland: sprinters = power / speed with a longer preparatory phase; distance swimmers = stability and endurance of shoulder girdle, hips and core
Masters swimmers need strength training (shoulder protection, bone density, recovery with age)
